page: The UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-16GB is a compute-focused virtual server provisioned on a KVM hypervisor. It runs on the 64-bit x86 architecture using an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The instance delivers 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with single-thread-per-core sizing. The processor subsystem includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates comprehensive vector extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory is provisioned at 16.0 GB, resulting in a density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio characterizes a compute-oriented allocation. Storage is provided as a bundled 200 GB local SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server does not include any GPU accelerators, dedicating all onboard compute capacity exclusively to x86_64 CPU operations.

In synthetic performance evaluations, the instance demonstrates standout single-core compute results. It achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core tests (3671.98), single-threaded gzip compression (38.12 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (17.51 GB/sec). Multithreaded execution aligns with the mid-tier cloud distribution, recording a Geekbench multicore score of 6962.0 and PassMark CPU score of 17608.73. Conversely, memory subsystem metrics are a visible tradeoff: PassMark memory ranks in the lower tier (1601.92), and larger model inference (7B parameters) exhibits weak throughput, with text generation dropping to 5.45 tokens per second. Static web serving reaches 11.74 GB/sec, while Redis achieves 8.9 million SET operations per second.

Given its dense vCPU allocation, bundled SSD storage, and strong single-core performance relative to its shared-core resource profile, the server is cost-effective for CPU-centric tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools. Typical best-fit workloads include CI/CD build environments, software compilation with clang, data compression pipelines, microservices, and static or compute-driven web serving. Workloads requiring large in-memory caches, big data analytics, or large language model inference are restrained by the 16 GB memory ceiling.
